karty.priklad: Dw i'n siŵr taw ei hagwedd hi yw'r broblem.
karty.priklad_cs: I'm sure it's her attitude that's the problem (agwedd → [h]agwedd after ei = her).
karty.mnemo: An AGgro (AG-wedd) attitude: a face as red as a red-hot poker.

extra.pozn: agwedd at = attitude towards (soft mutation after at); own example, emphatic sentence with taw (p. 176)

sever.priklad: Dw i'n siŵr mai ei hagwedd hi ydy'r broblem.
sever.priklad_cs: I'm sure it's her attitude that's the problem (agwedd → [h]agwedd after ei = her).
sever.pozn: north: mai instead of taw (L14), ydy instead of yw (L5)

karty.priklad: Darllenodd Mari ei cherdd hi yn yr Eisteddfod.
karty.priklad_cs: Mari read her poem at the Eisteddfod (cerdd → [ch]erdd after ei = her).
karty.mnemo: A poem set to a CHORD (CERDD) on the harp, recited by the red dragon breathing fire.

extra.pozn: cerddor = musician (L17), cerddorfa = orchestra (L2), on the same theme bardd = poet; in the book Cerdd gan Emyr Davies (p. 179); own example

karty.priklad: Dw i ddim wedi cael ateb i fy nghwyn i.
karty.priklad_cs: I haven't had an answer to my complaint (cwyn → [ngh]wyn after fy).
karty.mnemo: A complaint to the QUEEN (CWYN), posted in a red pillar box.

extra.pozn: cwyno = to complain (L2, function: complaining); own example

karty.priklad: Mae nyth fach yn y goeden.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a little nest in the tree (bach → [f]ach after the feminine nyth; coeden → [g]oeden after y).
karty.mnemo: BeNEATH (NYTH) the branches, a red kite sits on its nest.

extra.pozn: nythu = to nest; feminine according to the coursebook, dictionaries (GPC) mostly give masculine: stick to the coursebook, check; own example

karty.priklad: Mae tagfa fawr ar yr M4 y tu allan i Gaerdydd.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a big jam on the M4 outside Cardiff (mawr → [f]awr after the feminine tagfa; Caerdydd → [G]aerdydd after i).
karty.mnemo: tagu (to choke) + -fa (place): the place where you choke – among miles of red brake lights.

extra.pozn: the ending -fa = place (mynedfa L6, cerddorfa L2); sentence from the dialogue Tagfa, p. 182

karty.priklad: Dw i'n meddwl taw taran glywais i fan 'na.
karty.priklad_cs: I think it was thunder I heard there (clywais → [g]lywais after the emphasised object).
karty.mnemo: A drum roll – TA-RAN! – and the whole sky flashes red.

extra.pozn: mellt a tharanau = thunder and lightning (taranau → [th]aranau after a); mellten = lightning (L5); sentence from the dialogue Tagfa, p. 182

sever.priklad: Dw i'n meddwl mai taran glywais i fan 'na.
sever.priklad_cs: I think it was thunder I heard there (clywais → [g]lywais after the emphasised object).

karty.priklad: Roedd torf fawr yn y stadiwm.
karty.priklad_cs: There was a big crowd in the stadium (mawr → [f]awr after the feminine torf).
karty.mnemo: Sounds like TURF: a crowd in red shirts stampeding across the turf.

extra.pozn: Geirfa L14 (p. 171); also in the news glossary, section Chwaraeon (p. 263); own example

karty.priklad: Does dim amynedd gyda fi heddiw.
karty.priklad_cs: I've got no patience today.
karty.mnemo: "Just A MINute (AMYN-edd)!" – waiting patiently, still as a snowman.

extra.pozn: amyneddgar = patient, diamynedd = impatient (outside the coursebook); own example

sever.priklad: Does gen i ddim amynedd heddiw.
sever.pozn: north: Does gen i ddim instead of Does dim … gyda fi (L6)

karty.priklad: Mae'r ciw yn enfawr erbyn hyn.
karty.priklad_cs: The queue is huge by now.
karty.mnemo: From English queue: a long queue in the frost, everyone blue with cold.

extra.pozn: ciwio = to queue; sentence from the dialogue Tagfa, p. 182

karty.priklad: Mae'r crys 'ma wedi'i wneud o gotwm.
karty.priklad_cs: This shirt is made of cotton (cotwm → [g]otwm after o).
karty.mnemo: From English cotton: cotton wool piled like snow in a frosty shop window.

extra.pozn: other materials: sidan = silk (L5), gwlân = wool (L10), lledr = leather (L15); own example

karty.priklad: Talwch wrth y cownter, os gwelwch yn dda.
karty.priklad_cs: Pay at the counter, please.
karty.mnemo: From English counter: the counter of a blue ice-cream van.

extra.pozn: own example

karty.priklad: Rhowch eich manylion cyswllt ar y ffurflen.
karty.priklad_cs: Put your contact details on the form.
karty.mnemo: cysylltu (to contact, to connect) → cyswllt: a contact number scribbled on a frosted window.

extra.pozn: cysylltiad = connection (L6); mewn cyswllt â = in contact with; the coursebook gives no plural; manylion personol = personal details (Robin Radio, p. 185); own example

karty.priklad: Mae deiet iach yn bwysig iawn.
karty.priklad_cs: A healthy diet is very important (pwysig → [b]wysig after yn).
karty.mnemo: From English diet: nothing on the plate but one pea and a blue ice lolly.

extra.pozn: on the same theme bwyta'n iach = to eat healthily; own example

karty.priklad: Mae diweithdra wedi codi eto eleni.
karty.priklad_cs: Unemployment has gone up again this year.
karty.mnemo: di- (without) + gwaith (work): without work – the factory gates frozen shut all winter.

extra.pozn: di-waith = unemployed; in the news glossary, section Byd gwaith (p. 263); own example

karty.priklad: Dw i'n meddwl taw diffyg hyder sy'n ei stopio fe.
karty.priklad_cs: I think it's a lack of confidence that's stopping him.
karty.mnemo: Confidence makes you stand HIGHER (HYDER) – right at the top of the ski lift.

extra.pozn: diffyg hyder = lack of confidence (Robin Radio, p. 185); diffyg (L9); hyderus = confident; own example

sever.priklad: Dw i'n meddwl mai diffyg hyder sy'n ei stopio fo.
sever.priklad_cs: I think it's a lack of confidence that's stopping him.
sever.pozn: north: mai instead of taw (L14), fo instead of fe (L1)

karty.priklad: Mae'r heddlu'n ymchwilio i ladrad yn siop Dillad Del.
karty.priklad_cs: The police are investigating a burglary at the shop Dillad Del (lladrad → [l]adrad after i).
karty.mnemo: lleidr (thief) → lladrad: a burglary on a freezing night, footprints left in the frost.

extra.pozn: lleidr/lladron = thief/thieves (L11); on the same theme dwyn = to steal; the shop Dillad Del from Bwletin Newyddion (p. 184); own example

karty.priklad: Beth yw lluosog 'tŷ'? – Tai.
karty.priklad_cs: What's the plural of 'tŷ'? – Tai.
karty.mnemo: llu (host, multitude) + -og: a whole host of them – like hailstones.

extra.pozn: unigol = singular; table and the poem Lluosog on p. 179

sever.pozn: north: Be ydy instead of Beth yw (L5)

karty.priklad: Mae'r lori wedi gollwng ei llwyth ar y ffordd.
karty.priklad_cs: The lorry has shed its load on the road.
karty.mnemo: A whole LOAD (LLWYTH) of frozen peas spilled across an icy road.

extra.pozn: llwyth also = tribe (plural llwythau); colloquially llwyth o = loads of; sentence based on the dialogue Tagfa, p. 182

karty.priklad: Dw i'n gwybod taw Fflur yw'r rhedwr cyflyma.
karty.priklad_cs: I know that Fflur is the fastest runner.
karty.mnemo: rhedeg (to run) + -wr: a runner in a blue vest, breath steaming on a frosty morning.

extra.pozn: grammatically masculine even for a woman (rhedwraig = female runner); Fflur from the table on p. 175; own example

sever.priklad: Dw i'n gwybod mai Fflur ydy'r rhedwr cyflyma.
sever.priklad_cs: I know that Fflur is the fastest runner.
sever.pozn: north: mai instead of taw (L14), ydy instead of yw (L5)

karty.priklad: Mae rhedwr traws gwlad yn rasio ar drac mwdlyd.
karty.priklad_cs: A cross-country runner is racing on a muddy track (trac → [d]rac after ar).
karty.mnemo: From English track: a running track white with frost.

extra.pozn: traws gwlad = cross-country (L14); sentence based on p. 173

karty.priklad: Mae'r heddlu'n apelio am dystion.
karty.priklad_cs: The police are appealing for witnesses (tystion → [d]ystion after am).
karty.mnemo: TYST ~ TEST: the witness's story is put to the test under a cold shower of questions.

extra.pozn: grammatically masculine even for a woman; tystiolaeth = evidence, testimony; apelio am = to appeal for (L4); in the news glossary, section Trosedd (p. 263); own example

karty.priklad: Beth sy'n awgrymu bod lladron yn gweld y siop fel targed hawdd?
karty.priklad_cs: What suggests that thieves see the shop as an easy target?
karty.mnemo: "OH, GRIM (AW-GRYM)!" – he suggests something with a grim face.

extra.pozn: awgrym = suggestion, hint; sentence from Bwletin Newyddion, p. 184

sever.priklad: Be sy'n awgrymu bod lladron yn gweld y siop fel targed hawdd?
sever.priklad_cs: What suggests that thieves see the shop as an easy target?

karty.priklad: Roedd y lori'n cludo pren.
karty.priklad_cs: The lorry was carrying timber.
karty.mnemo: The lorry transports its load in a CLOUD (CLUD-o) of exhaust.

extra.pozn: cludiant = transport; on the same theme trafnidiaeth = traffic, transport (L16); sentence based on the dialogue Tagfa, p. 182

karty.priklad: Cafodd y bardd ei goroni yn yr Eisteddfod.
karty.priklad_cs: The poet was crowned at the Eisteddfod (coroni → [g]oroni after ei = his).
karty.mnemo: coron = crown (Latin corona).

extra.pozn: at the Eisteddfod the winner of the free-verse competition is crowned, cadeirio (L13) = to chair the winner in strict metre; passive with cael (L11); own example

karty.priklad: Cymysgwch y menyn â thipyn o siwgr.
karty.priklad_cs: Mix the butter with a little sugar (tipyn → [th]ipyn after â).
karty.mnemo: cy- + MYSG ~ MIX: mix it all in one bowl.

extra.pozn: pattern cymysgu â; cymysg = mixed; own example

karty.priklad: Fi sy'n delio â chwynion y cwsmeriaid.
karty.priklad_cs: I deal with the customers' complaints (cwynion → [ch]wynion after â).
karty.mnemo: From English deal.

extra.pozn: pattern delio â; emphatic sentence with sy (L13); own example

karty.priklad: Mae Siân yn gweini ar gwsmeriaid yn y caffi.
karty.priklad_cs: Siân serves customers in the café (cwsmeriaid → [g]wsmeriaid after ar).
karty.mnemo: The waiter serves WINE (GWEINI).

extra.pozn: gweini ar = to serve someone; gweinydd = waiter (L2); the phrase gweini ar from the exercise on p. 173; the stem gwein- (gweinwch, gweinodd) is outside the coursebook, check; own example
